steps.content:
10 Minutes
Until the Trial
You and Demon entered the courtroom.
The commissioner, the FAC official, and the City Council's chief judge were already in their seats. As high officials of various departments, they were all familiar faces to you.
The man in the hat was also present, but he didn't seem to be welcome.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: Why is the 9th Agency getting involved? This isn't your style.
The man didn't respond to the commissioner's hiss, but he tipped his hat to you in respect.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Staff
steps.content: Long time no see, Chief. Are you all prepared?
Fifteen days ago, you met him for the first time. The man claimed that the 9th Agency he represented could help.
At the time, he simply said he would provide extra evidence and information to help you win the case.
To your surprise, the most mysterious spy agency in DisCity got personally involved and placed one of their own in the jury.
You were planning to chat before the trial, but the judge began striking the gavel.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Staff
steps.content: Seemed like some people couldn't wait.
The judge was a bigwig in his sixties or seventies from the municipal court. He didn't give you a chance to chat, and began to speak.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: Defendant Demon Schilder, accused of killing thirteen high officials including Abel Schilder and Dole Young, will be tried by this court.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: Court is in session.
The strike of the gavel echoed throughout the courtroom.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: The commissioner began to speak.
The commissioner adjusted his spectacles. You recognized him. A month ago, it was this rising star from Eastside's legal world who gave you the files and Vera's bracelet.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: Ladies and gentlemen, since this is not a regular court, and everyone is familiar with this case, I will summarize the details in a short and concise manner.
The commissioner waved the files in his hand.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: Taking the case of former Special Task Force Vice Captain Finn as an example, the fingerprints and the murder weapon can be perfectly matched, and the surveillance footage from the victim's home recorded the entire crime.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: All the other cases had similar circumstances. He didn't accidentally leave behind evidence of his crimes, he flaunted them on purpose to spread fear.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: The crimes committed by Demon Schilder have had an extremely egregious impact. The City Council, and indeed all the citizens of Eastside, cannot accept him to be simply taken under MBCC custody.
The commissioner paused, looked around, then gazed at you and Demon with his head raised.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: On behalf of the City Council, I demand the MBCC to hand over Demon Schilder to be publicly executed.
After the commissioner finished his cold statement, the entire room went silent. Everyone looked at you with malice.
Frowning, Demon tried to speak several times, but couldn't bring himself to open his mouth.
Before he could finally talk, the judge noticed his intentions.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: Defendant, it's not your turn to speak.
Even though the commissioner said nothing else, and the jurors were all curious about what Demon had to say, the judge did not give Demon a chance to defend himself.
Perhaps Demon's trial eight years ago was also like this.

options: Help Demon get a chance to speak

choices.text: Help Demon get a chance to speak

steps.content: Was this the case eight years ago, too? The defendant doesn't even get a chance to speak? This doesn't seem like a proper trial.
If you want the Bureau to hand him over, we have to at least hear what he has to say.
The judge frowned. He didn't expect you to talk back. After a while, he spoke again.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: Defendant Demon, what was your motive for killing the thirteen victims?
Under your pressure, the City Council backed down. The judge took the initiative to "question" Demon.
Demon's eyes showed a hint of panic. It was obvious that his past trauma had a profound impact on him.
You put a hand on his shoulder.
Don't worry. I'll help you.
Demon took a deep breath and shifted his gaze to the commissioner.

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: Twelve of them...
Demon's voice was barely audible.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: What did you say?

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: Eight years ago, the twelve of them murdered Abel...

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: I killed them to exact revenge.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: Oh?
The commissioner wiped the corners of his eyes somewhat dramatically and continued.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: Are you saying that it wasn't you who shot and killed Abel Schilder in Rose Hall eight years ago? And that it were the twelve deceased whom you killed later?

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: No... I was the one who shot Abel.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: Then did those twelve instruct you to kill Abel?
The commissioner interrupted Demon several times, throwing in various theories to disrupt Demon's testimony.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: Objection overruled. The commissioner is just doing his job.
Demon glared at the judge, but failed to change his mind.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: ${PlayerName}, control your Sinner.
The court's malicious intent was disgusting. There was no hint of justice in this trial from beginning to end.
Fortunately, you were well prepared. As long as you set the pace, you could break the game.
Don't be distracted by his questions. Tell only necessary information.
Demon looked at you, and began to speak again.

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: I shot Abel because he had already mutated into a Corruptor and was attacking innocent civilians. I had no other choice.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: That is to say, you admit to shooting and killing Councilor Abel Schilder, your foster father, on July 6th, 104?

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: During his speech, thugs armed with Mania weapons burst into the hall and attacked indiscriminately.

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: Abel was hit... though he didn't die on the spot, he quickly mutated and lost his consciousness...

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: I'm sorry, everyone.
The commissioner interrupted Demon again.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: Since we mentioned Abel Schilder, it's necessary to reiterate the details of that case.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: On such an important matter, the defendant's account will inevitably omit certain details, which will mislead everyone's judgment. Allow me.
The commissioner looked around. Nobody objected. He cleared his throat and began to speak.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: On the night of July 6th, 104, the victim Abel was giving a campaign speech at Rose Hall when four thugs barged in and committed a massacre. Security personnel later shot and killed them.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: While the victim was being escorted to safety, Demon used a 9mm pistol to shoot the victim six times in the head. The victim died on the spot.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: The murder weapon was recovered at the scene of the crime. Eyewitness testimonies, fingerprints, DNA testing, and bullet analysis all point to the fact that you're the killer, Demon Schilder.
The commissioner ended his long monologue with a smug smirk.

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: I already said that Abel had turned into a Corruptor and was attacking innocent civilians...

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: It's true that according the report, Abel Schilder's body showed a high degree of mutation. The four thugs were also indeed armed with Mania weapons...

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: However, eight years ago, Mania weapons were extremely rare. In all of Eastside, no agency other than the Special Task Force could access such dangerous weapons.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: Coincidentally, the defendant Demon was the Captain of the Special Task Force at the time... Back then, nobody except for senior Special Task Force members had access to Mania weapons. Isn't that right?
The commissioner looked over at the FAC official.
The FAC official frowned silently for a while.

steps.speaker: FAC Official
steps.content: Early Mania weapons were indeed accessible to the Special Task Force.

steps.speaker: FAC Official
steps.content: After the incident, the FAC conducted an internal investigation, which concluded that four Mania weapons were missing from the inventory.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: I think the truth is clear. Defendant Demon Schilder stole the Mania weapons and gave them to the thugs.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: He also sent away Special Task Force members responsible for guarding the venue to allow the thugs to enter without hindrance...

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: Where's the evidence?
Demon interrupted the droning commissioner.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: All the case details come from the Special Task Force's internal testimonies.

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: Testimonies?

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: In the absence of other conclusive physical evidence, oral testimonies are sufficient to make a conviction.

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: I have some "conclusive physical evidence."

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: The fake document where Finn forged my signature is in Room 1102 of the West End Apartments.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: It's pointless of you to mention a random name and address like that.

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: Haha... are all Eastside commissioners as incompetent as you?

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: The name belongs to the person you just mentioned, former Vice Captain Finn.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: ...Are we going to wait here for several hours for someone to fetch it?

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: It won't take that long.

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: ...Are you scared?
Sweat drops formed on the commissioner's forehead.
However, the bang of the gavel put an end to the confrontation.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: The evidence mentioned by the defendant had not been submitted to the court beforehand.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: Therefore it cannot be used in the trial.
The atmosphere in the courtroom instantly dropped to the freezing point.

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: ...When did you ever give me the chance to submit evidence?

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: The rules of the courtroom haven't changed for twenty years. You should've read it up before you came, Demon.

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: I remember... eight years ago, you sentenced me to death...

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: That's right.

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: I should've paid you a visit a long time ago.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: You have no more chances.
The judge rejected your request to submit evidence outright, ending the fiery confrontation.
Demon stopped arguing, and just stared coldly at the judge. He no longer had any hope for a fair trial.
Demon's attempts seemed to have failed, but you still had to try.
Abel was Demon's foster father. From what we know, they had a good relationship. Demon has no reason to kill him...

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: On this point, we also have contradicting evidence.
The commissioner spoke up again.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: We obtained the defendant Demon Schilder's transfer records from Eastside Bank.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: On June 29th, 104, Demon's private account received a huge payment from an anonymous account.
The commissioner looked at the judge.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: Defendant Demon Schilder, please explain where this payment came from.
Demon kept silent, without any intention to answer.
This was a question you could not answer for Demon. You didn't know anything about it.

options: Tell Demon not to give up

choices.text: Tell Demon not to give up

steps.content: Don't give up.
Even if they don't accept our new evidence, there must be flaws with their existing evidence... we still have a chance.
Under your coaxing, Demon's attitude seemed to thaw.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: Defendant, answer the question.
The judge urged him to answer again. A look of annoyance and disgust flashed on Demon's face.

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: ...I don't know.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: You don't know? So you cannot explain where this payment came from?

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: I only have one personal account, and my sister Vera took care of it.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: Are you saying that Vera instructed you to kill her biological father?

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: Shut up!
Demon immediately sprung up in anger—Vera was his last family member. He couldn't allow anyone to frame his sister like that.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: Thank goodness Miss Vera is under our care. Otherwise, I highly suspect you'd try to hurt her, too.
The City Council was finally showing its true colors.

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: I knew it... you took Vera...

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: Miss Vera has requested our protection since January 105. She is hiding from your murderous pursuit.

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: Where is she?!

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: I'm sorry, but in the interests of Miss Vera's safety, she will not be testifying in person today.
The commissioner took out a thin plastic bag.

steps.speaker: Comissioner
steps.content: But before the trial began, we attained her testimony, which proves all your crimes in the past eight years.

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: Impossible!
Demon roared.

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: Vera is a family, there's no way she would...

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: Watch your tongue, Demon Schilder.
The judge's voice was like a bucket of ice-cold water dousing out Demon's flames of rage.
With Vera in their hands, Demon didn't dare fight back.
You realize that the City Council's trump card was Vera. They were holding her hostage to coerce Demon into pleading guilty.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: The testimony states that you plotted to murder Councilor Abel Schilder. Defendant Demon, how do you plead?
Demon's eyes were bloodshot, and his tightly clenched jaw made a horrible grinding noise.

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: ...plead guilty.
His words were engulfed by utter hatred and unwillingness.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: You're accused of murdering twelve city councilors. How do you plead?

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: I... plead guilty.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: You forced the victim Vera Schilder to take the blame for Abel's murder, and tried to murder her every chance you got in the past eight years. How do you plead?
The trial was heading towards the worst possible outcome. If this went on, Demon would surely be doomed.
You said you'd help him... you promised... but under the circumstance...

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Staff
steps.content: My apologies. Allow me to interrupt.
The man from the 9th Agency suddenly spoke up.
The judge's face went dark. He didn't expect someone to interrupt him at the most critical moment.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Staff
steps.content: I'd like to ask... Commissioner, when was this testimony recorded?
The commissioner looked at the judge in slight confusion.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: Two days ago.
The judge didn't dare hide that fact in front of the agent from the notorious 9th Agency.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Staff
steps.content: Who conducted the questioning and transcription of the testimony?

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: This was a matter of utmost importance, so I completed the entire procedure myself.
Faced with the current situation, the seasoned judge grew impatient. He just wanted to answer the spy's questions quickly and finish the trial.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Staff
steps.content: Oh? How strange...
The man put on a teasing tone.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Staff
steps.content: Five hours ago, my men raided a secret Black Water outpost. You should know what I mean by Black Water.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Staff
steps.content: We found quite a few corpses there. Just now, we conducted DNA analysis and confirmed the identity of one of the bodies...

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Staff
steps.content: Councilor Abel Schilder's daughter, Vera Schilder.
Hearing this, Demon stiffened, and his eyes became listless.
His teeth chattered, but he was unable to say a single word.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: That's... impossible...

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Staff
steps.content: I advise you not to lie about her date of death. Miss Vera has been dead for at least six years.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: No... no... that's not...

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Staff
steps.content: Are you trying to say that you were unaware of Miss Vera's death? Or that Black Water concealed the information? Who is your contact with Black Water? Would you like to come to the morgue with me?
The judge finally fell silent, his face turning ashen. He knew it was useless to say anything now.
In just a few words, the trial took a one-eighty degree turn - all thanks to the man from the 9th Agency.
He wore a faint smile on his face.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Staff
steps.content: The trial for the murder of Eastside's city councilors is hereby suspended. Defendant Demon Schilder shall return to the MBCC for confinement.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Staff
steps.content: The main goal now is to investigate the fraud committed by the City Council and weed out Black Water's infiltration... Lord Blake, please come with me.
Emerging as the victor, he slowly strut over to the judge and gestured for him to leave.
You realized now that the conversation seven days ago and his offer to help was part of a well-planned scheme. The 9th Agency took advantage of both you and Demon.
The entire trial was just a cover for the 9th Agency to overthrow the City Council.

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: Why...
Demon's voice was hoarse. He should be the center of attention at the trial, but at this moment, the courtroom was chaotic. No one noticed him except you.
He sat frozen on the floor, his voice trembling.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Staff
steps.content: I'm sorry for your experience, Demon.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Staff
steps.content: But your trial has concluded, and we have more important things to attend to...

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: What did Vera do... why did you do this to her...
The judge looked over. His face was grim, but he still forced himself to croak in defense.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: It had nothing to do with me...

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: You said... you transcribed her testimony...

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: Did you really believe that?

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: It wasn't my decision alone to hand her over to Black Water. We lost contact with her afterward.
But you dared to use her name to fabricate evidence?
The judge's face turned ashen.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: Nobody wanted her dead... It's just that I didn't expect Parma to act so boldly.

steps.speaker: Demon
steps.content: ...It's not important anymore.
Everything happened so quickly. You saw everything, but there was no time to stop it.
Demon broke free from the heavy shackles and pounced on the judge. The next moment, the judge's head fell to the ground with a thud.
It took a full five seconds for everyone else to realize what happened. Demon slumped to the floor like a puppet cut from its strings. His pupils lost focus, as if his soul had left his body.
Eight years later, Demon committed another murder in public.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Staff
steps.content: Um...
Sorry. I couldn't stop him.
And your investigation?

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Staff
steps.content: It's fine. We got enough justification already. Anyway, thanks for your cooperation.
He glanced at the commissioner paralyzed in fear on the floor, and then at Demon.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Staff
steps.content: Demon is an unstable pawn. Please be careful with him.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Staff
steps.content: A murder in broad daylight is not easy to placate. You must deal with it appropriately, otherwise you won't be able to stop people from talking.
I will take care of it.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Staff
steps.content: I trust your judgment. Oh, by the way...

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Staff
steps.content: Miss Langley says hi.
The man tipped his hat in respect one last time and left. Next, the FAC official took a deep look at Demon and left silently as well.
In the hall, only you, Demon and a roomful of carnage remained.
